items.title: Lemma 12.13
items.statement_scope: Whole result on physical p.65: let (X, O_X) be a derived complex analytic space and let 1 denote the final object of X. Then there exists an effective epimorphism of the form coproduct_i U_i -> 1 in X together with a collection of closed immersions (X/U_i, O_X) -> Spec_Tan(C^{n_i}); the printed statement adds 'where each M_i in Tan is a complex manifold' after Spec_Tan(C^{n_i}) and is preserved as printed.
standard_prerequisites: Lemma 11.11 (this work, physical p.59): closed-immersion criterion used to conclude f' is a closed immersion
Definition 12.3 and Construction 12.5 (this work, physical pp.61-62): Tan-structure and Spec_Tan formalism
Remark V.2.3.4 (DAG-V, external standard prerequisite; not in this PDF): factorization through Spec_Tan(U)
items.difficulty_reason: H2 under author-work-bearing-core-v1-20261114: the proof is a concrete non-routine construction, not a routine verification. After reducing to X = Shv(X) and working locally, it chooses a closed immersion (X, pi_0 O_X^alg) -> (U, O_U^alg) with U a subset of C^n, uses global sections f_1,...,f_n to build f : (X, O_X) -> Spec_Tan(C^n), factors f through Spec_Tan(U) by Remark V.2.3.4, and applies Lemma 11.11 to conclude the resulting map f' is a closed immersion (author physical p.65). This bears the Tan-structure/closed-immersion argument actually carried by this unit.

difficulty_evidence.bearing_core: Local construction of closed immersions (X/U_i, O_X) -> Spec_Tan(C^{n_i}) by selecting a closed immersion into (U, O_U^alg), forming f from global sections f_1,...,f_n, factoring through Spec_Tan(U) via Remark V.2.3.4, and applying Lemma 11.11 to obtain a closed immersion.
